title: Sirenboard: compact dedicated-capacity controls & health canvas
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, operator-focused dashboard (codename: Sirenboard) for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces multi-signal health, quick autoscale/burst controls, and contextual cost impact. The goal is a single-line, high-density canvas for on-call engineers and SREs to triage capacity events and apply safe, reversible scaling actions without leaving the console.
background: Current Dedicated pool pages are detailed but overloaded for fast incident triage. Incident responders want fewer clicks, clearer safe-action affordances, and immediate visibility into what will change to cost/SLOs. We must balance a compact surface with guardrails to prevent accidental large-scale changes.
design_goals: Single-line health strip per pool showing latency, queue depth, utilization, thermal signal
Inline burst presets and one-click canary ramp-up with preview of token cost delta
Compact action drawer with preflight checks and automatic rollback option
Accessible keyboard interactions and mobile responsiveness for on-call use
Telemetry hooks: each action emits an audit event and links to a runbook
deliverables: High-fidelity interactive prototype (Figma) for dev handoff
Design spec page with UX flows, edge cases, and accessibility notes
A/B test plan for rollout to 20% of Dedicated accounts

Audit event emitted for every action with linkable runbook; action drawer includes rollback button
open_questions: Should burst presets be per-pool or account-wide? PM prefers per-pool, but Ops wants global templates.
How to surface GPU topology details (e.g., mixed-slot pools) without cluttering Sirenboard?
Exact signal thresholds for green/amber/red on latency and queue depth need SRE alignment
